clue.text: American's ready to resist

definitions.meaning: in American slang a ... is a dollar, ready money

explanation.surface: An American says they are prepared to put up a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a buck is a dollar in US slang, and to buck is to oppose.

clue.text: Rejection making British leave quickly

parts.note: to rush off is to depart in haste

explanation.surface: A Briton who storms out is giving someone a snub.
explanation.definitionFit: A curt dismissal of someone's approach is a form of refusal.

clue.text: Traveller, one involved in china and metal

indicators.note: the traveller and one are wrapped inside the china word

parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, a chum
a Rom is a Romany, a traveller
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A traveller deals in porcelain and metal goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' looks like porcelain, but it is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard, shiny element used for plating is one of the metals.

clue.text: One whose livelihood is in other people's hands

definitions.text: One whose livelihood is in other people's hands

parts.words: One whose livelihood is in other people's hands
parts.note: read literally, this worker earns a living by holding and tending clients' fingers and nails

explanation.surface: Someone whose income depends on the goodwill of others.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail technician literally works with customers' hands all day.

clue.text: A legal action not reaching conclusion in courts

indicators.note: the word for legal action loses its final letter

parts.note: a trial is a legal action in court

explanation.surface: A lawsuit that never gets to a verdict in the law courts.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is an open central court of a building, and this is the plural.

clue.text: Imprisoned patriarch for crime exploiting employer

parts.note: to be inside is to be in prison
Job is an Old Testament patriarch

explanation.surface: A church leader is jailed for defrauding his own organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A theft carried out by staff at their own workplace is called this.

clue.text: After loveless marriage inform one man it's stupid

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, O, so the word for marriage loses its O

parts.note: a union is a marriage
to tell is to inform
I is the Roman numeral for one
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: Telling a man after an unhappy wedding that he is a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' removes O (love, a nil score in tennis) from UNION, leaving UNIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking intelligence is a plain synonym for being dim.

clue.text: Liable to be knocked down in attack

definitions.meaning: standing in the road, one may be run over

explanation.surface: Someone vulnerable to being floored in a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Two readings: split in two, a position where traffic may hit you; as one word, an advance or raid.

clue.text: Recovering from breakdown, unsettled after short time

indicators.note: the debt word comes after the time abbreviation

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a bill owing is unsettled

explanation.surface: Someone recuperating from a collapse, still anxious after a brief while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breakdown' suggests a nervous collapse, but means a broken-down vehicle being pulled away.
explanation.definitionFit: A tow truck hauling a broken-down car is getting it back from the roadside.

clue.text: Against current university voting scheme I have run

parts.note: PR is proportional representation, an electoral system
I have contracts to I've
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A student debating society proposes a new electoral method.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling against the current of a river means heading towards its source.

clue.text: A meat serving I changed as result of this, possibly

definitions.text: A meat serving I changed as result of this, possibly

indicators.note: changing the letters means arranging them anew

explanation.surface: A diner swaps the meat dish because of their diet.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet without meat could explain why someone swapped out a meat course.

clue.text: Youngster gets into second quarrel in bad part of town

indicators.note: the youngster's word is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a row is a quarrel
a kid is a youngster

explanation.surface: A child becomes involved in a dispute in a rough neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-down urban area full of down-and-outs is known by this name.

clue.text: Made rough revision in volunteer force

indicators.note: revising the letters means reordering them into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone produced a rough draft while serving in a volunteer unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' looks like a description of the revision, but it is part of the letters to rearrange. The HOME GUARD was Britain's World War II volunteer defence force.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's wartime local defence force was made up of unpaid volunteers.

clue.text: A number in company with American author

explanation.surface: Someone in a group alongside a writer from the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: The old word for two, and the pen name of the author Samuel Clemens.

clue.text: Equivalent of third of May as national holiday

definitions.text: Equivalent of third of May as national holiday

parts.words: Equivalent of third of May as national holiday
parts.note: Poland's Constitution Day falls on 3 May; the parallel holiday in the USA is Independence Day

explanation.surface: A question about which date matches a Polish national celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: American Independence Day, celebrated in midsummer, plays the role Constitution Day does in Poland.

clue.text: Drink provided by William's home help, we hear

indicators.note: says the phrase is judged by its sound

parts.note: William of Orange's home is Orange, and help is aid

explanation.surface: A drink served by William's housekeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: William III, William of Orange, takes his title from Orange; ORANGE + AID sounds like the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy citrus soft drink is a type of beverage.

clue.text: Way old dope becomes cause of illness

parts.note: a path is a way
gen is slang for information, as is dope

explanation.surface: A street drug turns out to make people ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like a drug, but means information: GEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ or virus that brings on disease is called this.

clue.text: A French boyfriend is inconstant

parts.note: un is French for a
a steady is a regular boyfriend

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's lover proves fickle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a French boyfriend, but 'A French' is the French word for 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wavering and not firm is a close synonym for changeable.

clue.text: Genius captures Italian island for us

indicators.note: the phrase for genius takes the Italian abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a great brain is a genius

explanation.surface: A brilliant person seizes an island in the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for us' signals that the island is home to the British setter and readers.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of the British Isles is the home island of a Times setter.

clue.text: Again beat sportsman up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: re is a prefix meaning again
to flog is to beat

explanation.surface: Someone beats a sportsman up a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of a club-and-ball sport is a sportsman.

clue.text: Cure for misrule, at least partly

definitions.text: Cure for misrule, at least partly

indicators.note: the answer sits partly within the words just before

explanation.surface: Correcting bad government, if only a little.
explanation.definitionFit: Improving a corrupt system through change is a remedy for bad rule.

clue.text: Piano used in old-time musical performance

indicators.note: the piano letter is placed within the old-time letters

parts.note: O for old plus ERA for time
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: An old upright piano features in a nostalgic music-hall show.
explanation.definitionFit: A staged dramatic work set to music and sung is a kind of musical performance.

clue.text: Ammunition that's got right shape to scatter

indicators.note: scattering the letters throws them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Shot shaped correctly so that it spreads out on firing.
explanation.definitionFit: Small iron balls packed together and fired from a cannon were a type of munition.

clue.text: Quickly providing a courteous expression of disagreement

parts.note: pace, Latin for with peace, means with due respect to someone you disagree with

explanation.surface: Disagreeing politely, but at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving at a fast rate means swiftly, an adverb like quickly.

clue.text: Growing things outside Idaho in another state

indicators.note: the plant word goes around the state abbreviation

parts.note: flora are plants, things that grow
ID is the postal abbreviation for Idaho

explanation.surface: Plants grown beyond Idaho's borders, in a different part of the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sunshine State is one of the American states, a different one from Idaho.

clue.text: Island in Caribbean, as opposed to one in Pacific? Not quite

parts.note: anti means against or opposed to

indicators.note: the island name stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: Guam is an island in the western Pacific

explanation.surface: Comparing a Caribbean island with an almost-matching Pacific one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the final M from GUAM, leaving GUA.
explanation.definitionFit: An island in the Leeward group, part of the nation with Barbuda, lies in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Party man's broken reed, yet not overlooked

indicators.note: the reed is split apart to take another word inside

parts.note: a party man is a member of a political party

explanation.surface: A party politician proves a broken reed, though people still notice him.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'broken reed' is an idiom for someone unreliable; here 'broken' means REED is opened up as RE...ED to hold MEMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept in mind and recalled, rather than forgotten, is the opposite of overlooked.

clue.text: Starts off months before December, finishes in April/May —- just

parts.note: the starts of October and November, the months before December

indicators.note: the final letters of each part of April/May are taken

explanation.surface: Something begins in autumn and ends in late spring, and only just.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts off' takes the first letters of October and November, O and N; 'finishes in' takes L and Y from April and May.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb, merely or no more than: a synonym in the sense of barely.
